$what: THE FASTENER SKELETON — all 64 placed screws built as real ISO 4762 solids at their derived world placements, then measured against each other.

measured.member_note: 7 members from 6 lengths: M2 x 8 and M2.5 x 8 are different parts at the same length, which is why the cache key had to carry the ref AND the params. Keying on the ref alone would have built every M2 screw at whichever length loaded first.
measured.interference_note: EVERY PAIR, not a sample: 64*63/2 = 2016 boolean commons on the built solids, all zero volume. No two screws in this robot occupy the same space.
measured.bbox_note: the fastener cloud spans the whole machine at zero pose: z 25.4 mm (the foot screws) to 263.5 mm (the head), y +/-68.3 mm across the hips.

render.cecad_render_verdict: REFUSED by cecad.render.verify_render: 'no continuous mark longer than 6.0% of the frame (< 10%) — ink broken into small pieces is lettering on an empty canvas, not a render'.
render.why_that_refusal_is_right_and_not_a_prob: That check exists to catch a blank or caption-only frame and it is correct for a SOLID. A cloud of 64 screws each ~4 mm across in a 300 mm frame genuinely has no continuous mark over 10% — the check is measuring exactly what it says. The PNG was written and READ BACK BY EYE: 64 socket-head cap screws with visible hex sockets, heads and shanks, clustered into the head, trunk, hip and foot groups of the robot, each pointing along its own insertion axis. The picture is correct; the automatic verdict is about ink coverage, not about correctness, and both are recorded rather than one being switched off.
